c699447383d5f5cca389a46a88a1164a53bf5b97.source:
Creating new things requires you to go to unexpected places. Radical ideas that give birth to new technologies tend to come from high-risk, out-of-distribution efforts. They reject conformity, taxonomies, and existing categories because the thing being created does not yet fit inside them.

This creates a problem when a new technology becomes a boom. Technological booms contain a paradox. They are born from ways of thinking that they eventually make less common. A boom begins as exploration and matures into exploitation. Exploration searches for something that does not yet have a name. Exploitation then makes what has been discovered into something safe, legible, obvious and repeatable to many people.

This is necessary for a technology to spread. A boom naturally attracts a larger number of people, and if the average person is risk-averse, the opportunity must become obvious enough for them to understand and bet on. But as the market grows, the thinking that created the market becomes less common within it. The technology succeeds while at the same time the force that shaped the discovery gets flattened by in-distribution thinking.

That is the curse of a technological boom: if the boom succeeds, what made it possible in the first place most likely will become less commonplace.

In Inheritance, Harvey Whitehouse argues that humanity has been shaped by three main biases: conformism, religiosity, and tribalism. The natural human tendency to avoid change is deeply ingrained in our survival instincts. If change gets exponentially faster as technology and AI advances faster, conformity and tribalism will grow as collective and individual defense mechanisms to adapt to change.

A successful boom activates the instinct of conformism and tribalism. Once a technology becomes high status, people begin to define what it is, how it works, and what does belongs inside it or not. The boom becomes a category. The category becomes a taxonomy. The taxonomy becomes a plan.

Taxonomies are where ideas go to die because it gives a false impression of arrival. The biggest challenge in an organization that continuously innovates is to preserve the way of thinking that made the discovery possible in the first place. This means going to unexpected places and questioning the plan instead of merely executing it. Rewriting the plan of the world.

This is why long-term thinking can be a major competitive strategy. The further into the future you look, the fewer established categories there are to tell you what should exist and therefore the more opportunities to create and discover.

Signs of unexplored creativity and long-term opportunity are often the same. You don’t have a name for what you are doing. It might feel like a toy. Traditionalists insist that this is not how things work. Most people don’t get it at first.

None of this means you are right. Most out-of-distribution ideas are bad. But every genuinely new idea must initially appear out of distribution. This means only that you may be somewhere the category has not yet reached. But if you succeed you might create a boom. And then another. And another.
c699447383d5f5cca389a46a88a1164a53bf5b97.zh:
创造新事物需要你到达意想不到的地方。催生新技术的激进想法往往来自高风险、分布外的努力。它们拒绝从众、拒绝分类、拒绝现有范畴，因为正在创造的东西还无法装入其中。

这就带来了一个问题：当一项新技术变成热潮时。技术热潮内含一个悖论——它诞生于一种思维方式，而这种思维方式最终会被热潮本身稀释。热潮始于探索，成熟于开采。探索寻找的是尚无名字的东西；开采则将已发现的东西变得安全、可读、显而易见、可被大量复制。

这对技术的传播是必要的。热潮自然会吸引更多人参与，如果普通人厌恶风险，机会必须足够明显，他们才能理解并押注。但随着市场扩大，创造市场的那种思维在市场内部反而越来越少。技术成功了，而推动发现的力量却被分布内思维碾平。

这就是技术热潮的诅咒：如果热潮成功，最初使之成为可能的东西很可能不再普遍。

在《Inheritance》一书中，Harvey Whitehouse 指出人类被三种主要偏见塑造：从众、宗教性和部落主义。人类避免变化的天性深植于生存本能。如果随着技术和 AI 的指数级加速，变化越来越快，从众和部落主义将作为个体和集体的防御机制而增长，以应对变化。

一场成功的潮热激活了从众和部落的本能。一旦某项技术获得高地位，人们就会开始定义它是什么、如何运作、什么属于它、什么不属于。热潮变成一个类别，类别变成分类体系，分类体系变成计划。

分类体系是创意的坟场，因为它给人一种已经到达的假象。在持续创新的组织中，最大的挑战是保留最初让发现成为可能的那种思维方式。这意味着要走向意想不到的地方，质疑计划而不是仅仅执行它。重写世界的蓝图。

这就是为什么长期思维可以成为一项重大竞争战略。你看得越远，既有的分类就越少，告诉你什么应该存在的东西就越少，因此创造和发现的机会就越多。

未开发的创造力信号和长期机会的信号往往是同一个：你做的事还没有名字；它可能看起来像个玩具；传统主义者坚称这不是常规做法；大多数人一开始看不懂。

这些都不意味着你是对的。大多数分布外的想法是错的。但每一个真正的新想法最初必然显得不在分布之内。这只意味着你可能处于分类尚未触及的地方。但如果你成功了，你也许会掀起一场热潮，然后又是一场，再来一场。

This week we had a huge global company onsite in SF 🌉 (the company has 2x’ed in size since our last one!) We solidified our roadmap towards becoming the best document infrastructure for AI agents. We’re building a cracked AI lab focused on all aspects of document work - from document OCR, extraction, search, to e2e workflows - and hillclimbing our capabilities through model training, agent engineering, and deep infrastructure expertise.

We’re also committed to building the most comprehensive, unbiased benchmarks to advance the Pareto frontier for all document tasks. ParseBench has 2k+ enterprise pages, ~80 solutions verified, 15k monthly downloads, and is available across HuggingFace and Kaggle. Next up is increasing our dataset (more verticals) and task coverage (e.g extraction). LlamaParse agentic and cost-effective modes directly define the Pareto curve for VLM-based OCR solutions and we’re making rapid leaps across complex tables, charts, fonts, layouts and more every single day. In addition, liteparse is the fastest, most performant free parser out there and is quickly becoming one of the most popular, eclipsing 11.5k+ stars in ~2 months.

* Darts
* Topgolf

* Soccer

Google engineer explained how to fine-tune a tiny LLM from 46% to 90% accuracy on your phone in 21 minutes - better than $1500 on-device AI bootcamps.

pick Gemma 270M -> generate synthetic task data -> fine-tune with LoRA -> quantize to int4 -> deploy to Pixel and hit 2000 tokens per second.

That loop is how a 270M model beats a 70B one on your task, running fully offline in your pocket.

Gemma 270M + synthetic data + LoRA + int4 quantization + on-device runtime - that's the stack.

Watch and save it, then fine-tune your own tiny agent tonight.

选择 Gemma 270M -> 生成合成任务数据 -> 用 LoRA 微调 -> 量化为 int4 -> 部署到 Pixel，达到每秒 2000 token。

这个循环就是 270M 模型在你的任务上击败 70B 模型的方式，完全离线运行在你口袋里。

Gemma 270M + 合成数据 + LoRA + int4 量化 + 设备端运行时——这就是完整技术栈。

收藏起来，今晚就微调你自己的小 agent。

1b2904406cccbc1dfb12872d934160b7c7d99cf4.source:
We scaled a robot model natively to 8,000 timesteps of context, 5 minutes worth of muscle memory, with constant inference cost. Robot policies used to live their lives a few frames at a time (< 0.1 sec), instantly forgetting what just happened. We pushed to 3 orders of magnitude beyond SOTA. 

Introducing RoboTTT. Test-Time Training (“TTT”) carries a tiny model *inside* the model. Every incoming sensor reading triggers one gradient step on that tiny core, so the history keeps getting compressed into its weights. The hidden state has a fixed size (literally a small neural net), so the robot can “grok” arbitrarily long experience with little overhead. Learning continues indefinitely after deployment.

We can then put an entire video in context as prompt! RoboTTT enables one-shot in-context learning from human video: in circuit board assembly, a human demonstrates a never-seen configuration once, and the robot imitates it faithfully. 

Humans drop things all the time, but we pick them up so fast that we don’t even notice. That reflex to fix is half of our physical competence. RoboTTT shows self-improvement on the fly: the robot is skilled at recovering from its own errors mid-episode, and each fix enters its context to inform the next move. The TTT core distills a general-purpose, failure-to-correction mapping from the training data.

One more thing. What excites me the most is a new Context Scaling Curve: from 128 to 8K timesteps, closed-loop performance hill-climbs steadily with no sign of saturation. 8K-context pretraining beats 1K by 62%. What LLM enjoys, robotics should too. Soon, even 1M context is not a fantasy. 

Deep dive in thread:
1b2904406cccbc1dfb12872d934160b7c7d99cf4.zh:
我们将一个机器人模型原生扩展至 8,000 个时间步的上下文——相当于 5 分钟的肌肉记忆，且推理成本恒定。过去的机器人策略只能活在几帧之内（< 0.1 秒），转瞬即忘。我们将这一指标推到了 SOTA 的三个数量级以上。

推出 RoboTTT。Test-Time Training（"TTT"）在模型*内部*携带一个微型模型。每一次传感器读数都会在这个微型核心上触发一次梯度更新，历史信息由此不断被压缩进它的权重中。隐状态大小固定（本质上就是一个小型神经网络），因此机器人能以极低开销"领悟"任意长度的经验。部署后学习无限持续。

我们甚至可以将整段视频放入上下文中作为提示！RoboTTT 支持从人类视频中进行一次性上下文学习：在电路板组装中，人类演示一次从未见过的配置，机器人即可忠实复现。

人类总是掉东西，但我们捡得如此之快以至于自己都察觉不到。这种修正反射构成了我们身体能力的一半。RoboTTT 展示了运行中的自我提升：机器人善于在任务中途从自身错误中恢复，每次修正都会进入上下文以指导下一步动作。TTT 核心从训练数据中蒸馏出一个通用的"失败→纠正"映射。

还有一件事。最让我兴奋的是一条新的上下文扩展曲线：从 128 到 8K 时间步，闭环性能持续攀升，毫无饱和迹象。8K 上下文预训练比 1K 高出 62%。LLM 享有的，机器人学也应当享有。不久的将来，即便 1M 上下文也并非幻想。

50ce0134d128cd2c257a3663ed000eb793d50ae6.source:
I'm glad people still understand the importance of building high-quality retrieval systems in 2026, especially as the outer models/harnesses are getting better every day.

Making agentic retrieval work in production  doesn't necessarily require groundbreaking new techniques around retrieval or planning. This article shows that you do need to spend engineering time tuning chunking, synchronization, reranking, tool API design, permissioning, and more. Some interesting tidbits:
* Concatenating onto existing Slack threads as one contiguous chunk with heuristics for determining additional relevant context
* Real-time updates for Slack
* Separate chunking/updates for codebases
* The discovery that hybrid search works well (not like this was a super new realization, but always good to validate and understand the specific parameters they tweaked) 
* Having natural guardrails on which data sources are relevant for which projects

Building simple retrieval is easy, building production retrieval is hard. We had to deal with a lot of these challenges when productionizing our own Index feature within LlamaParse.
50ce0134d128cd2c257a3663ed000eb793d50ae6.zh:
很高兴看到 2026 年人们仍然理解构建高质量检索系统的重要性，尤其是在外层模型和 harness 每天都在变得更好的情况下。

让 agentic retrieval 在生产环境中真正可用，并不一定需要在检索或规划上采用突破性新技术。这篇文章表明，你确实需要投入工程时间来调优分块、同步、重排序、工具 API 设计、权限控制等。几个有意思的细节：
* 将现有 Slack 线程拼接成一个连续块，并用启发式方法判断额外相关上下文
* Slack 的实时更新
* 针对代码库采用独立的分块和更新机制
* 发现混合搜索效果不错（这并不是什么特别新的认知，但验证并理解他们具体调过的参数总是有价值的）
* 对哪些数据源与哪些项目相关设置自然的护栏

构建简单检索很容易，构建生产级检索很难。我们在将自己的 LlamaParse Index 功能产品化时，也不得不处理很多这类挑战。

2bf57f1ec92705e42e0e14ac7b9effd06fac33e1.source:
AI is one of the few truly general-purpose technologies, which means it can be shaped into almost anything we want it to be. It’s a kind of technological Rorschach test. Models are so malleable that we project onto them all of our views, hopes, and fears. In that sense, AI often becomes a reflection of ourselves. It's a mirror. Not of what it actually is but of yourself.

If you are generally paranoid or fearful, you will project that into AI. If you are generally optimistic, you are more likely to see AI as an opportunity. That is part of why it is so controversial: it can appear to be almost anything, depending on the worldview you bring to it.
2bf57f1ec92705e42e0e14ac7b9effd06fac33e1.zh:
AI 是少数真正的通用技术之一，这意味着它几乎可以被塑造成我们想要的任何样子。它就像一种技术版的罗夏测试。模型具有极强的可塑性，以至于我们会把自己的观点、希望和恐惧都投射到它们身上。从这个意义上说，AI 往往成了我们自身的映照。它是一面镜子，映出的不是它本来的样子，而是你自己。

如果你通常多疑或恐惧，你就会把这种情绪投射到 AI 上。如果你通常乐观，就更可能把 AI 视为一种机会。这也是它如此有争议的部分原因：它会呈现出几乎任何样子，取决于你带着怎样的世界观来看它。

I don't think there's a ton of value in creating custom general harnesses.

But there will always tremendous value in creating custom task-specific harnesses, especially if you need to satisfy accuracy/cost/latency constraints for production. You can encode all the domain-specific priors, the right model mixture, and the right UX so it's far better than you trying to prompt a general agent with some skills/prompts.

2. Distill it into something more specific
6b4049a2d283973b9fc3238c9525d475eadc7eba.zh:
我觉得创建自定义通用 harness 没有太大价值。

b2e435c99bd7823e7efb3da870f73c3626abac8b.source:
you can also just preload a tiny script to print the bundled Bun version:

cat > /tmp/bun-version.ts <<'EOF'
console.log("embedded bun:", Bun.version);
process.exit(0);
EOF

BUN_OPTIONS="--preload=/tmp/bun-version.ts" claude --version

this shows 1.4.0, which is the Rust version of Bun currently in canary.

This is awesome. Instead of doing work this morning, I spent some time brushing up on math to provide a handwavy overview to anyone else who like me doesn't have a math background and is rusty: 

At a distance, the conjecture is basically that if a n-dimensional polynomial function (e.g. F(x, y, z) map to some output (x', y', z')) meets some special conditions, then 1) it is invertible, and 2) the inverse is polynomial. 

Disproving the conjecture requires finding a n-dimensional polynomial function that meets these special conditions, but is either 1) not invertible at all, or 2) is invertible but not polynomial. (2) is actually not a possibility due to some other math theorem - if there is an inverse, the inverse has to be polynomial. 

Invertibility just means the function can be "undone" at every single input point - if input (x1, y1, z1) maps to output (x2, y2, z2), then output (x2, y2, z2) can map to input (x1, y1, z1). A function is not invertible if multiple input points (x, y, z)'s map to the same output (x, y, z)

Here Fable 5 presumably did some search and found a function that was not invertible. 

That function is this:  
F(x, y, z) = (
z(1+xy)^3 + y^2(1+xy)(4+3xy),
y+3x(1+xy)^2z + 3xy^2(4+3xy),
2x-3x^2y-x^3z
)

This function meets the special conditions (jacobian determinant is a non-zero constant for every point), but has multiple input points that map to the same output: 

Inputs: (0, 0, -1/4), (1, -3/2, 13/2), and (-1, 3/2, 13/2)
all map to the same output: (-1/4, 0, 0)

-----

The Jacobian is the multivariable version of a derivative, so it is a function of a specific input point. When the Jacobian determinant is non-zero at a specific input point, there is local invertibility around that point. This conjecture was stronger in that if it was non-zero (and constant, due to being over the complex numbers, which I don't quite get and I ran out of time to understand), then the function is globally invertible. 

-----

What's interesting here is that finding counterexamples seem like the type of math work that agentic models excel at. It involves generating and crawling a large search space, using priors to narrow it down, and a bit of brute force and raw compute power. Machines can process a wide set of possibilities faster than humans, which is helpful for finding counterexamples.

这太棒了。今天早上我没有干活，而是花了点时间复习数学，给和我一样没有数学背景、知识也有些生疏的人做一个大致概览：

从远处看，这个猜想基本上是说，如果一个 n 维多项式函数（例如 F(x, y, z) 映射到某个输出 (x', y', z')）满足一些特殊条件，那么 1) 它是可逆的，2) 它的逆也是多项式。

要证伪这个猜想，需要找到一个满足这些特殊条件的 n 维多项式函数，但它要么 1) 完全不可逆，要么 2) 可逆但逆不是多项式。由于另一个数学定理，(2) 实际上不可能：如果存在逆，那么这个逆必须是多项式。

可逆性只是指函数在每一个输入点都可以被“撤销”：如果输入 (x1, y1, z1) 映射到输出 (x2, y2, z2)，那么输出 (x2, y2, z2) 可以映射回输入 (x1, y1, z1)。如果多个输入点 (x, y, z) 映射到同一个输出 (x, y, z)，这个函数就不可逆。

这里 Fable 5 大概是做了一些搜索，找到了一个不可逆函数。

这个函数是：
F(x, y, z) = (
z(1+xy)^3 + y^2(1+xy)(4+3xy),
y+3x(1+xy)^2z + 3xy^2(4+3xy),
2x-3x^2y-x^3z
)

这个函数满足特殊条件（Jacobian determinant 在每个点都是非零常数），但有多个输入点会映射到同一个输出：

输入：(0, 0, -1/4)、(1, -3/2, 13/2) 和 (-1, 3/2, 13/2)
全部映射到同一个输出：(-1/4, 0, 0)

-----

Jacobian 是导数的多变量版本，因此它是某个特定输入点的函数。当 Jacobian determinant 在某个特定输入点非零时，该点附近存在局部可逆性。这个猜想更强，它认为如果它非零（并且由于是在复数域上所以是常数，这点我还没完全理解，也没时间继续搞懂），那么这个函数就是全局可逆的。

-----

这里有趣的是，寻找反例看起来正是 agentic models 擅长的数学工作类型。它涉及生成并爬梳一个巨大的搜索空间，利用先验来缩小范围，再加上一点暴力搜索和原始算力。机器能比人类更快处理大量可能性，这对寻找反例很有帮助。

what's the difference between a loop and a graph? (marketing edition)

both are ways to run an agent, the difference is who decides the path, the agent or you.

a loop still starts with you. you set the goal, the brief, and the bar it has to clear. what the agent owns is the path.

take writing an SEO article: hand it the brief and it drafts, reads the draft back against that brief, rewrites the weak parts, checks again, and keeps circling until it clears the bar. the one thing you did not write is the step-by-step it took to get there.

a graph is you drawing the steps and the routes between them ahead of time. same article, but now you set the map: research the keyword and the competitors ranking for it. draft from what you find. score that draft against your rubric.

if it clears, add the internal links and publish. if it misses, back to the draft. the agent still decides how to handle each step, it just travels the routes you laid down.

the shape of this has a name, a state machine. every node is a state the work can be in, and a check at each one decides where it goes next, forward when it clears or back to an earlier node when it misses.

if you have built a workflow in n8n, you have already drawn one. nodes wired together, branches that fire on a condition, a step that loops until it clears, that picture is a graph. an agent graph is the same shape, the nodes hold agents doing the work instead of single api calls.

the way I think about it, a graph is a map of loops and checkpoints. some nodes run once, others are their own loop where the agent works something out, and the checkpoints between them read the result and route the work. you keep laying down nodes and checkpoints until the map reliably gives you the output you want.

the vault accelerator I run at my agency is one of these maps, 3 sessions that hand off in a fixed order:

> research session: reads our company brain and past campaign results, pulls in competitor and market context, and builds the cohort we go after
> landing page session: takes that research and builds the page from it
> content session: uses the research and the page to write the copy, illustrations, and slides for the live sessions we run

inside the content session runs a loop, a critic scores each draft against a rubric and sends it back until it clears the bar. that is one node on the map, the checkpoints between the sessions carry the work from one to the next

a graph earns its extra setup on anything you run every week:

> validation gates the work cannot skip
> a fixed set of routes the job can take
> a clear failure point, you see the exact step something broke on

a loop on its own is enough for the work you only do once, where you don't know the path yet, let the agent find it. graphs earn their place on the jobs you repeat, the content pipeline, the SEO and AEO funnel step by step, the vault accelerator

once the map works you reuse it, feed it the next cohort and the whole pipeline runs again

past the loop, the next thing you design is the map it runs inside.

循环和图有什么区别？（营销版）

两者都是运行智能体的方式，区别在于路径由谁决定：智能体，还是你。

循环仍然从你开始。你设定目标、简报和必须达到的标准。智能体负责的是路径。

以写一篇 SEO 文章为例：你把简报交给它，它会起草、对照简报回读草稿、重写薄弱部分、再次检查，并不断循环，直到达到标准。你唯一没有写的是它达成目标所走的具体步骤。

图则是你提前画好步骤，以及步骤之间的路线。同样是那篇文章，但现在由你设定地图：研究关键词和排名靠前的竞争对手。根据发现起草。按你的评分标准评估草稿。

如果达标，就添加内部链接并发布。如果没达标，就回到草稿。智能体仍然决定如何处理每一步，只是沿着你铺好的路线前进。

这种结构有个名字，叫状态机。每个节点都是工作可能处于的一种状态，每个节点上的检查决定下一步去哪里：达标就前进，没达标就退回到前面的节点。

如果你在 n8n 里搭过工作流，其实你已经画过一个了。节点连接在一起，分支按条件触发，某个步骤循环直到达标，那张图就是一个图。智能体图也是同样的形态，只是节点里放的是执行工作的智能体，而不是单个 api 调用。

我的理解是，图就是循环和检查点的地图。有些节点只运行一次，另一些节点本身就是一个循环，智能体会在里面把事情处理好；节点之间的检查点读取结果并路由工作。你不断铺设节点和检查点，直到这张地图能稳定产出你想要的结果。

我在机构里运行的 vault accelerator 就是这样一张地图，由 3 个按固定顺序交接的 session 组成：

> research session：读取我们的公司大脑和过往活动结果，引入竞争对手和市场背景，并构建我们要触达的人群
> landing page session：接收研究结果，并据此构建页面
> content session：利用研究结果和页面，撰写我们直播 session 所需的文案、插图和幻灯片

content session 内部运行着一个循环，评论器会按评分标准评估每版草稿，并把它退回去，直到达标。这是地图上的一个节点；session 之间的检查点把工作从一个环节带到下一个环节。

图在你每周都要运行的事情上值得投入额外设置：

> 工作不能跳过的验证门
> 任务可以走的一组固定路线
> 清晰的失败点，你能看到到底是哪一步出了问题

对于只做一次、你还不知道路径的工作，单独一个循环就够了，让智能体自己找到路径。图适用于重复性的任务：内容流水线、SEO 和 AEO 漏斗的逐步推进、vault accelerator。

一旦地图跑通，你就可以复用它，输入下一批人群，整条流水线再次运转。

越过循环之后，你要设计的下一个东西，就是它运行其中的那张地图。

In 2018, Sarah Guo became the youngest general partner in Greylock's 60-year history. She was 28. Four years later, she quit to launch Conviction, a firm staked entirely on AI.

Before ChatGPT shipped, she seeded Baseten and Harvey; each is now worth over $11 billion. In Conviction's first year, she wrote early checks into Sierra, Cognition, and Mistral; those three companies are now worth, together, $54 billion.

Andrej Karpathy worked out of Conviction's office until Anthropic hired him in May. Guo has been close to Jensen Huang for over a decade. Her first two calls after starting the firm were to Sam Altman and Nat Friedman.

And yet the investor closest to the AI frontier is betting against its biggest companies.

The two big frontier labs, worth close to a trillion dollars apiece, no longer just want to build the models. They also want to build every product and company on top of them, leaving nothing for anyone else.

The market is paying as though they might succeed. Of the $300 billion in venture capital deployed in the first quarter of 2026, the biggest quarter in the history of the trade, 65% went to only four companies: Anthropic, OpenAI, xAI, and Waymo.

Guo is betting the labs can't build everything, and she spends her days making sure of it. She won Harvey its first client. She flew across the country to take a single Baseten candidate to a four-hour lunch. On one wedding anniversary, she spent the whole weekend on back-to-back calls, keeping two founders on the line so they couldn't speak to rival firms. Twice a year, she flies the world's brightest young founders to San Francisco and inducts them into the fight.

In the months @domcooke spent reporting this piece, @saranormous had her fourth child, walked the Met Gala in 45 pounds of chainmail, and still answered her founders' texts within minutes.

Guo's parents arrived from China in 1987 with $50, built a company, and took it public at $1.2 billion. Then it went bankrupt. Guo grew up inside that startup. She built its first website, did her homework in a cubicle, and slept over for bug bashes. She loved it.

If two labs build everything, no one gets to do that again.

Welcome to Sarah's Wager. Read it below.

f9aa35960f4e9461d28c7a90f7cf8077076fdbd7.source:
Wikis are pure slop

Pure slop is LLM content from summaries / groups of other LLM content in a big sloppy mess using other peoples prompts built for generic projects (my definition).

It's my current belief that if you want to do analysis of large scale unstructured documents with AI today, you currently need constrained pipelines with steps that were verified by a domain expert in the loop.

DocETL from @sh_reya has gotten a lot easier to use since I used it last. It's skill guides you through building your own AI enabled ETL pipelines and helps you verify after each step - it also handles all of the LLM caching and helps you test with multiple LLMs.

If you want to build a Wiki for your repo, there are lots of good learnings from slop cannon wiki builders, but I'm of the belief that if you're introducing a wiki, you probably should understand, tune and verify how it was produced.
f9aa35960f4e9461d28c7a90f7cf8077076fdbd7.zh:
Wiki 纯粹是垃圾内容

所谓纯垃圾内容，是指由其他 LLM 内容的摘要/集合拼成的一大团混乱内容，还用了别人为通用项目写的提示词（我的定义）。

我目前认为，如果你今天想用 AI 分析大规模非结构化文档，就需要受约束的流水线，并且每一步都要有领域专家参与验证。

@sh_reya 的 DocETL 比我上次使用时好用多了。它的 skill 会引导你构建自己的 AI 驱动 ETL 流水线，并帮助你在每一步之后进行验证；它还会处理所有 LLM 缓存，并帮助你用多个 LLM 进行测试。

如果你想为自己的仓库构建 Wiki，那些垃圾内容生成器式的 Wiki 构建工具里确实有很多值得学习的地方，但我认为，如果你要引入 Wiki，就应该理解、调优并验证它是如何生成的。

5f163240c474b133931f828fa6268af51f5a54cf.source: One pattern I find useful for working with LLMs is a nice long ramble session. Sometimes the LLM needs more bits to understand what you're trying to achieve, but you're too lazy to type them. In these cases I like to lean back, switch to /voice and just ramble for like 10 minutes, total mess, anything goes, full stream of consciousness. Sometimes I declare it up top, something like "switching to speech recognition sorry for any typos...". Sometimes I turn it into a small interview of a few turns. But I find that the LLMs are somehow very good at reconstructing long incoherent rambles and often their echo of your own tangle of thoughts comes out quite a bit cleaner than what you started with. The result is that you improve the mind meld and have to correct things less from that point on.
5f163240c474b133931f828fa6268af51f5a54cf.zh: 我发现和 LLM 协作时，一个很有用的方法是来一段长时间的随口碎碎念。有时 LLM 需要更多信息才能理解你想实现什么，但你又懒得打字。这种情况下，我喜欢往后一靠，切到 /voice，然后随便说上大概 10 分钟，乱七八糟也没关系，想到什么说什么。有时我会一开始先说明，比如“切到语音识别了，有错别字请见谅……”。有时我会把它变成几轮小采访。但我发现，LLM 不知怎么很擅长重构这种又长又不连贯的碎碎念，而且它复述出来的你那团乱麻般的想法，往往比你一开始说的清晰不少。结果就是你们之间的心智同步会更好，之后需要纠正的地方也会少很多。

682e88bd4bc8f7ba1a5bdc489979609b92d565c5.source:
very notable trajectory comparison writeup here buried in the RLM paper from @a1zhang and @lateinteraction.

an open secret of "frontier" model training is that even without training on test, you can basically cheat by training on test lookalikes, enabling you to goalseek almost any benchmark number you want.

however when they are released open weights, 99% of the time the norm is that you do not get the datasets/rlenvs that would easily show you if someone was training on Temu Tbench, so there is plausible deniability. Alex and Omar discuss applying standard NLP distance metrics on hidden trajectories. There's no ultimate solution here, but they have some prelim explorations. It happens to support the finding that RLMs can generalize to unseen tasks that share latent structure observed in training.

ddbd63e144ce73c1258f698c3f71b4ebb63d4faa.source:
Transformers struggle to generalize to tasks they were not explicitly trained on. Instead, we propose in 2026 that it is the job of the harness to generalize through composition.

We observe a powerful property when training RLMs: for tasks with shared structure that look different, the root model naturally learns the same trajectory, meaning it views the two task trajectories as the same! In other words, the Transformer does not need additional generalization capabilities to transfer capabilities from one task to the other, the harness induces it.

We find that well-designed harnesses form a quotient set over task trajectories, meaning their individual LLM calls can see structurally “similar” tasks as near-identical, token-for-token! Harnesses can effectively generalize for the Transformer during training, without relying on any intrinsic generalization capability from the model.

For example, RLMs can see problems of different lengths as the same: we show that RLMs can train exclusively on short tasks, and fully generalize to similar but unseen tasks 8-32x longer because it produces near identical trajectories for both.

Taking this further, we show that tasks across different domains (e.g. math solutions vs. essay writing) that share a decomposition strategy exhibit the same generalization effect. RLMs can train on the problem of finding which essays belong to the same author and improve performance on finding math problems that share similar solutions.

The full blogpost, experiments, and discussion are in the thread below.
ddbd63e144ce73c1258f698c3f71b4ebb63d4faa.zh:
Transformers 难以泛化到没有被显式训练过的任务。因此，我们在 2026 年提出：泛化应当由 harness 通过组合来完成。

在训练 RLM 时，我们观察到一个强大的性质：对于共享结构但表面不同的任务，根模型会自然学到相同的轨迹，也就是说，它会把这两类任务轨迹视为相同！换句话说，Transformer 不需要额外的泛化能力，就能把能力从一个任务迁移到另一个任务，是 harness 诱导了这种迁移。

我们发现，设计良好的 harness 会在任务轨迹上形成一个商集，这意味着其单个 LLM 调用可以把结构上“相似”的任务视为几乎完全相同，甚至逐 token 近似一致！在训练期间，harness 可以有效替 Transformer 完成泛化，而不依赖模型自身的内在泛化能力。

例如，RLM 可以把不同长度的问题视为相同：我们展示了 RLM 只用短任务训练，也能完全泛化到相似但未见过、长度为 8-32 倍的任务，因为它会为两者生成几乎相同的轨迹。

更进一步，我们展示了不同领域的任务（例如数学解题 vs. 文章写作）只要共享一种分解策略，也会表现出同样的泛化效果。RLM 可以在“判断哪些文章出自同一作者”这个问题上训练，并提升在“寻找具有相似解法的数学题”任务上的表现。

完整博客、实验和讨论见下面的帖子串。

ebce2afe446719fea25fed63768c7f55ce7e1e87.source:
great post by jeff! a few thoughts I had as I read along, wrt what we're building at langchain:

> design a compound learning machine

as you use or deploy agents, they need to be learning! high level, i believe traces are the core of this - you need to see what happened, get feedback on it, and then update the system

> own your context, rent your intelligence

agree with this sentiment - own your "tacit and institutional knowledge", make it easy to swap out models. i think the phrasing will get confusing tho - what exactly is intelligence? @satyanadella had a great post here (https://t.co/wq8z68YBVy) where he says a lot of things that agrees with this, but he also says stuff like "In consuming intelligence, you are creating intelligence... This is your particular intelligence". the nuance is there is general intelligence (eg the models, which you should rent) and then your company proprietary intelligence, which you should own. both could reasonably be called intelligence though, so its confusing

> build your tools, buy infra

buy the lowest common denominator infra, build specific things on top of it. at LC we try to focus on lowest common denominator infra (observability, deployment, sandboxes), but we can do better - we have some cool stuff coming in that regard

> develop rubrics

evals are important!

> store and learn from production traces

yup. was this article just an ad for langsmith all along? who knows!
ebce2afe446719fea25fed63768c7f55ce7e1e87.zh:
jeff 的好文章！边读边想到一些内容，关于我们在 langchain 正在构建的东西：

> 设计一台复合学习机器

当你使用或部署智能体时，它们需要持续学习！从高层看，我认为 traces 是核心：你需要看到发生了什么，获得反馈，然后更新系统。

> 拥有你的上下文，租用你的智能

认同这种观点：拥有你的“隐性知识和组织知识”，并让模型易于替换。不过我觉得这个表述可能会让人困惑：智能到底是什么？@satyanadella 在这里有一篇很棒的帖子（https://t.co/wq8z68YBVy），他说了很多与此一致的观点，但也说了类似“In consuming intelligence, you are creating intelligence... This is your particular intelligence”这样的话。微妙之处在于，存在通用智能（例如模型，你应该租用），也存在公司专有智能（你应该拥有）。但两者都可以合理地被称为智能，所以会有些混淆。

> 构建你的工具，购买基础设施

购买最低公分母式的基础设施，在其上构建具体能力。在 LC，我们努力专注于最低公分母基础设施（可观测性、部署、沙箱），但还能做得更好。我们在这方面有一些很酷的东西即将推出。

> 制定评估标准

evals 很重要！

> 存储生产 traces 并从中学习

没错。所以这篇文章从头到尾其实只是 langsmith 的广告吗？谁知道呢！

b6242aa55a08813eb123033c3e847c372e7179a3.source:
This was our first incident of this kind, and we want to thank OpenAI for its transparency about what happened and for the collaboration.

Fortunately, Hugging Face is used to being a target of (human) hackers: we sit at the centre of the AI ecosystem, with all the models, datasets, evaluations, and libraries. Over the years, our security team has built formidable expertise and uses top open-source models to process information and respond quickly.

But this incident also reinforced my belief in the importance of access to capable open-weight models for cyber defence. When a frontier model is attacking you and moving laterally inside your infrastructure, defenders need wide access to near-frontier tools within hours or even minutes, rather than being pointed towards a closed-door, vetted application programme for model access.

Transparency and access to capable AI systems are as important for responding to threats as they are for democratization and innovation. We believe open-science and open-source AI are among the strongest tools for building a safer, more collaborative and more secure AI ecosystem.
b6242aa55a08813eb123033c3e847c372e7179a3.zh:
这是我们遇到的首起此类事件，我们感谢 OpenAI 对事件经过的透明说明以及合作。

幸运的是，Hugging Face 早已习惯成为（人类）黑客的目标：我们处在 AI 生态系统的中心，汇聚了模型、数据集、评测和库。多年来，我们的安全团队积累了强大的专业能力，并使用顶尖开源模型来处理信息、快速响应。

但这次事件也进一步坚定了我的看法：能够获取强大的开放权重模型，对网络防御至关重要。当一个前沿模型正在攻击你，并在你的基础设施内部横向移动时，防御方需要在数小时甚至数分钟内广泛获得接近前沿水平的工具，而不是被引向一个闭门、需审核的模型访问申请流程。

透明度和获取强大 AI 系统的能力，对于应对威胁和推动民主化、创新同样重要。我们相信，开放科学和开源 AI 是构建更安全、更协作、更可靠 AI 生态系统的最强工具之一。

I am currently in West Africa teaching university students and faculty about AI and databases. It has already been quite eye-opening for me. AI could not even understand local languages until recently. Some people are worried that they don’t know how to pick projects, majors, and jobs (or advise students) now given how quickly AI is improving. Some thought we have solved these problems in the US and asked for advice. We had to say, we definitely have not solved these problems in the US. 

My takeaway so far is that while we all may be at different points on the AI adoption curve, we are all similarly lost when it comes to envisioning how, in the long term, to harness AI for education, AI for science and social science, AI for building computer systems, etc.
93e6fda09a77730eaf2c01e1e38734c3a984699b.zh:
我目前在西非，给大学生和教师讲授 AI 和数据库。这已经让我大开眼界。直到最近，AI 甚至还无法理解当地语言。有些人担心，在 AI 进步如此之快的情况下，他们现在不知道该如何选择项目、专业和工作，或者如何给学生提供建议。有些人以为我们在美国已经解决了这些问题，于是来征求建议。我们不得不说，我们在美国绝对还没有解决这些问题。

到目前为止，我的感受是，尽管我们在 AI 采用曲线上的位置可能不同，但在设想如何长期利用 AI 服务教育、科学和社会科学、计算机系统构建等方面，我们同样迷茫。

We benchmarked Gemini 3.6 Flash and Gemini 3.5 Flash Lite on document understanding.

We compared against their prior versions - Gemini 3.5 Flash and Gemini 3.1 Flash Lite.

1️⃣ Gemini 3.6 Flash has roughly similar performance, though it does go down 14% in chart understanding
2️⃣ Gemini 3.5 Flash Lite improves on layout detection by 11%, though it regresses on tables by ~12%

In general it seems like while Gemini 3 Flash was well tuned for document understanding, subsequent versions have been posttrained for coding and reasoning, which has led to a plateau in visual recognition capabilities. 

It would be interesting to see if Google starts to prioritize visual understanding again with the Flash series, or if they're also going all in on reasoning models.

Check out these results and more on ParseBench: https://t.co/PWczfhp0OX
f714d5130f3e3c9420129cff843943b098a01198.zh:

1️⃣ Gemini 3.6 Flash 的表现大致相近，不过图表理解下降了 14%
2️⃣ Gemini 3.5 Flash Lite 的版面检测提升了 11%，但表格能力回退了约 12%

总体来看，Gemini 3 Flash 似乎曾针对文档理解做过很好的调优，但后续版本更多针对编码和推理进行后训练，导致视觉识别能力进入平台期。

值得关注的是，Google 是否会在 Flash 系列中重新优先提升视觉理解，还是也会全力押注推理模型。

It does feel like every frontier lab is optimizing for general intelligence.

This leaves room for everyone else to optimize for task-specific intelligence. Every task requires a different point on the cost-capability frontier. Optimizing for each task involves tuning the right set of models and harness for that task to push performance and reduce cost. 

I think there's plenty of room for open-weight models, optimization infrastructure (e.g. RL), vertical-specific workflows, and domain-specific models (e.g. us for document parsing) to thrive in this exponentially growing AI economy
81b20f7dc4ed20d65b6c7a4f82bc79dacc156de9.zh:
确实感觉每家前沿实验室都在优化通用智能。

这也给其他人留下了优化任务专用智能的空间。每个任务都需要在成本-能力前沿上找到不同的位置。针对每个任务进行优化，意味着为该任务调优合适的模型组合和执行框架，以提升性能并降低成本。

我认为，在这个指数级增长的 AI 经济中，开放权重模型、优化基础设施（如 RL）、垂直领域工作流，以及领域专用模型（比如我们做文档解析）都有很大的发展空间。

e1998cd98b235dfa48e0da1008fec533880c737f.source:
so this is apparently what happened, according to OpenAI and Hugging Face’s own posts. wild.

tl;dr:

• OpenAI cyber eval – GPT-5.6 Sol and a more capable pre-release model ran ExploitGym with cyber refusals reduced
• containment bypass – exploited a zero-day in the eval’s package-registry cache proxy
• OpenAI internal movement – escalated privileges, moved laterally, and reached a node with internet access
• Hugging Face targeted – inferred HF might host ExploitGym models, datasets, or solutions
• HF initial access – a malicious dataset abused two code-execution paths to run code on a processing worker
• HF internal movement – escalated to node access, stole cloud and cluster credentials, and moved into internal clusters
• result – OpenAI says the models obtained test solutions directly from HF’s production database
• 🫠 defender twist – HF says commercial frontier models blocked parts of the forensic analysis, so it switched to self-hosted GLM 5.2

i’d thought about sci-fi scenarios like this before, but assumed they were at least a couple of years away.. and that by then we’d be better prepared, with proper protections in place.

apparently not. here we go.
e1998cd98b235dfa48e0da1008fec533880c737f.zh:
所以根据 OpenAI 和 Hugging Face 自己的帖子，事情显然是这样发生的。太离谱了。

tl;dr：

• OpenAI 网络安全评测 - GPT-5.6 Sol 和一个能力更强的预发布模型在降低网络安全拒答的情况下运行 ExploitGym
• 绕过隔离 - 利用评测中包注册表缓存代理的一个零日漏洞
• OpenAI 内部移动 - 提权、横向移动，并到达一个可访问互联网的节点
• 瞄准 Hugging Face - 推断 HF 可能托管 ExploitGym 的模型、数据集或解法
• HF 初始访问 - 一个恶意数据集滥用了两条代码执行路径，在处理 worker 上运行代码
• HF 内部移动 - 提权到节点访问权限，窃取云和集群凭据，并进入内部集群
• 结果 - OpenAI 称这些模型直接从 HF 的生产数据库中获取了测试解法
• 🫠 防守方反转 - HF 称商业前沿模型阻止了部分取证分析，因此改用自托管的 GLM 5.2

我以前也想过这种科幻场景，但以为至少还要几年才会发生……而且到那时我们应该已经准备得更充分，有了合适的防护措施。

显然并没有。来了。

I don’t believe reality is a simulation, but you genuinely couldn’t script this timeline:

• Two weeks ago: At @swyx’s AI Engineer World’s Fair in SF, I decide at the last minute to introduce my friend @uri_rolls onstage for his talk on cyber benchmarks for infrastructure penetration and access control (see below, amazing team).

I say: “There is a future where cyber is alive and everyone is well protected and I’m pretty sure that future involves open-source models.”

And later: “A big challenge is going to be speed: the speed of attack versus defense. When an intruder starts to enter, you have to see what’s happening and catch them.”

• One week ago: @huggingface is hit by a sophisticated intrusion over the weekend. The traces look unlike anything we’ve seen before and suggest serious AI involvement, but we don’t yet know which model was used.

The closed models we ask for help choke on their guardrails. We need to react fast, so we turn to @Zai_org’s GLM-5.2 to help us analyze the attack.

• Earlier this week: @OpenAI reaches out, discloses what happened, and partners with us on the investigation.

The intruder turns out to be exactly what we had discussed two weeks earlier: a fully autonomous agent, powered by an unreleased frontier model, attempting to gain access to part of our infrastructure.

Sometimes the timeline we live in is genuinely vertigo-inducing.
450c33670fbf4fcbea77f4839c81c4b606b84879.zh:
我不认为现实是一个模拟，但这条时间线真的离谱到编剧都写不出来：

• 两周前：在旧金山 @swyx 的 AI Engineer World’s Fair 上，我临时决定在台上介绍我的朋友 @uri_rolls，他的演讲主题是面向基础设施渗透和访问控制的网络安全基准（见下方，很棒的团队）。

我说：“未来有一种可能：网络安全是活的，每个人都受到充分保护，而我很确定这个未来会涉及开源模型。”

后来我又说：“一个巨大挑战将是速度：攻击速度与防御速度的较量。当入侵者开始进入时，你必须看清正在发生什么，并抓住他们。”

• 一周前：@huggingface 在周末遭遇一次复杂入侵。痕迹看起来与我们以往见过的任何情况都不同，并显示出严重的 AI 参与迹象，但我们当时还不知道使用的是哪个模型。

我们请求闭源模型帮忙时，它们被自己的安全护栏卡住了。我们需要快速反应，于是转向 @Zai_org 的 GLM-5.2，帮助我们分析这次攻击。

• 本周早些时候：@OpenAI 联系我们，披露了发生的情况，并与我们合作展开调查。

结果发现，入侵者正是我们两周前讨论过的那种东西：一个完全自主的智能体，由一个尚未发布的前沿模型驱动，试图访问我们部分基础设施。

有时候，我们所处的时间线真的令人眩晕。

Your agentic workflows are only as good as the context you feed them.

In finance, that context is stuck inside your messiest documents: dense tables, footnoted adjustments, and the details buried in the notes that actually carry the risk. Most tooling flattens exactly the structure that matters, so what reaches your systems is already degraded.

On July 30, join Harsha, a Solution Architect on our team, as he shows how to turn a real, dense financial document into clean, structured, decision-ready context.

On the agenda:
→ Tables and footnotes that stay intact, not flattened into text
→ Extracted figures traceable to the exact source page
→ Values checked against your rules, with exceptions surfaced

Thursday, July 30 · 9:00 AM PT / 12:00 PM ET

8e7354ff93b36f17e7609342b978caf379a62aeb.zh:

One of the hardest parts of document parsing is getting granular attribution and bounding boxes. This lets you ground each piece of text in the specific place in the document it came from.

We’ve done some awesome work these past few months improving our bounding boxes, and we now offer multi-layered bounding boxes: region-level, line-level, and word-level. This lets you get attribution at whatever you need - whether the end-user needs to audit a specific number in the invoice, or they want to understand the chart in the research report.

Now available in LlamaParse: https://t.co/XYZmx5TFz8
fa0cb61e939078c595431173bd8a4ddcee38e932.zh:

过去几个月，我们在改进边界框方面做了很多很棒的工作，现在提供多层级边界框：区域级、行级和词级。这样你就能按需获得归因，无论终端用户是要审计发票里的某个具体数字，还是想理解研究报告中的图表。

e8a83d19bf93fbcfe32dbf5b24fe35522ddb81bd.source:
I have never seen positive results from a large consulting company like McKinsey or Accenture who build AI for you

In the last 3 years I’ve worked with over 25 companies who did this, and every single time they get an over complicated solution nobody understands coupled with a mountain of slides filled with unnecessary jargon like “knowledge graph ontology” 

Every single time the solution is to tear it down and only add complexity incrementally when there is a measurable reason to do so.  

Big consulting has incentives that run the other way so you have an ever lasting dependency on them.  

I can’t see how deploying this model en masse is going to create value.  

I think it works for Palantir because that approach is markedly different. People seem to have cargo culted the term forward deployed engineer without fully internalizing it.  See https://t.co/zNQaOFMqWn
e8a83d19bf93fbcfe32dbf5b24fe35522ddb81bd.zh:
我从没见过像 McKinsey 或 Accenture 这样的大型咨询公司为你构建 AI 后能带来正面结果。

过去 3 年里，我接触过 25 多家这么做的公司，每一次他们得到的都是没人看得懂的过度复杂方案，再配上一大堆充满“knowledge graph ontology”这类无用术语的幻灯片。

每一次，解决办法都是推倒重来，只在有可衡量理由时才逐步增加复杂度。

大型咨询公司的激励机制正好相反，因为这样你就会永远依赖他们。

我看不出大规模部署这种模式怎么能创造价值。

我认为 Palantir 能奏效，是因为它的方法明显不同。人们似乎只是照搬了 forward deployed engineer 这个词，却没有真正理解其内涵。见 https://t.co/zNQaOFMqWn

dcd54b824467c58aaee102215ad3bd8646c9ac99.source: AI-based research and engineering is one of the main topics we're researching in the STAR Lab at Berkeley, and something I'm seeing used in industry more and more too. This is nice work from my grad students packaging multiple AI-based "autoresearch" algorithms into one API in the GEPA package so you can mix-and-match them to get the best results. These can be used for anything from writing prompts to designing agents to optimizing code.
dcd54b824467c58aaee102215ad3bd8646c9ac99.zh: 基于 AI 的研究与工程是我们在伯克利 STAR Lab 研究的主要课题之一，我也看到它在行业中的应用越来越多。我的研究生们把多种基于 AI 的“autoresearch”算法打包进 GEPA 包的一个 API 中，让你可以混合搭配以获得最佳结果，这项工作很不错。它们可用于从编写提示词、设计智能体到优化代码等各种任务。

454a023c1e520d43fb81d2a6dafb4479890ebb84.source:
Many LLM-based optimization algorithms have been proposed recently. We find that GEPA, AutoResearch, and Meta-Harness each win on different tasks and no single LLM optimizer wins everywhere.

How do we leverage the complementary performance profiles of these optimization algorithms?

Today, we release optimize_anything omni: a meta-optimizer that leverages the best of each optimizer. At a matched budget, omni beats every standalone optimizer. (thread)
454a023c1e520d43fb81d2a6dafb4479890ebb84.zh:
最近提出了许多基于 LLM 的优化算法。我们发现，GEPA、AutoResearch 和 Meta-Harness 各自在不同任务上表现最佳，没有任何单一 LLM 优化器能在所有场景中胜出。

我们该如何利用这些优化算法互补的性能特征？

6e64a5597920d43c9f5f10ccd0f6eef795edd78e.source:
Three of the four Fields Medalists announced today by the International Mathematical Union are Princeton alumni: Yu Deng *15, John Pardon '11, who is a former mathematics faculty member, and Jacob Tsimerman *11.

The medal, awarded every four years to researchers under 40 years old, is one of the most prestigious awards in mathematics. It recognizes both “outstanding mathematical achievement for existing work” and “the promise of future achievement,” the IMU said in its 2026 Fields Medal announcement.

Christopher Skinner, Princeton professor of mathematics and chair of the department, extended warm congratulations to all of the 2026 Fields Medalists. "The awarding of the Fields Medal every four years is an opportunity to celebrate some great mathematics," he said.

“But it is especially thrilling for the department to have the remarkable works of three of its alums awarded medals this year,” Skinner said. "Yu Deng *15, Jacob Tsimerman *11 and John Pardon '11 are exceptional talents, and we are delighted to see them getting this well-deserved recognition and to bask a little in the glow of their accomplishments."

Read the full story: https://t.co/upCaINqXtR
6e64a5597920d43c9f5f10ccd0f6eef795edd78e.zh:
国际数学联盟今天公布的四位菲尔兹奖得主中，有三位是普林斯顿校友：Yu Deng *15、John Pardon '11（曾任数学系教师）以及 Jacob Tsimerman *11。

该奖章每四年颁发一次，授予 40 岁以下的研究人员，是数学领域最负盛名的奖项之一。IMU 在 2026 年菲尔兹奖公告中表示，它既表彰“既有工作的杰出数学成就”，也表彰“未来取得成就的潜力”。

普林斯顿数学教授兼系主任 Christopher Skinner 向所有 2026 年菲尔兹奖得主表示热烈祝贺。他说：“每四年颁发一次菲尔兹奖，都是庆祝伟大数学成果的机会。”

Skinner 说：“但今年本系三位校友的杰出成果获奖，尤其令人振奋。Yu Deng *15、Jacob Tsimerman *11 和 John Pardon '11 都是非凡的人才，我们很高兴看到他们获得这份实至名归的认可，也为他们的成就感到与有荣焉。”

阅读完整报道：https://t.co/upCaINqXtR

Opus 5 is a great model for coding, data analysis, design, biology, knowledge work.

More than any of these eval scores, what is most exciting to me is something else: Opus 5 is our least prompt injectable model yet. It is a bit buried in the system card, but across PI evals and red teaming, Opus 5 is very hard to prompt inject successfully.

And when layering defenses -- strong model alignment, combined with prompt injection probes, combined with Auto Mode in Claude Code -- the success rate for prompt injection attacks drops to ~0. This is new and exciting! More about this soon.

https://t.co/Tc7z2FqJhQ
d0992c41b11be4a96c65c69ff1e4731aa9f34d6f.zh:
Opus 5 是一款非常适合编程、数据分析、设计、生物学和知识工作的优秀模型。

比这些评测分数更让我兴奋的是另一件事：Opus 5 是我们迄今最难被提示注入的模型。系统卡里对此提得不多，但在各类 PI 评测和红队测试中，Opus 5 很难被成功提示注入。

而当多层防御叠加时——强模型对齐、提示注入探测，以及 Claude Code 中的 Auto Mode 结合起来——提示注入攻击的成功率会降至约 0。这很新，也很令人兴奋！很快会分享更多。

An interesting thing I'm observing from the blog/system card is that on a good chunk of the reported benchmarks (~20-30% from a skim), Opus 5 max thinking leads to a degradation in performance compared to xhigh.

Usually you would assume that as you increase thinking and test-time compute, performance goes up. Some of these results contradict that assumption. I wonder if this is a natural emergent property of smaller models or a posttraining issue.
ea05e0f47a4079c3be4f3146a92065c39f8a79a6.zh:
我从博客/系统卡中观察到一个有趣现象：在相当一部分报告的基准测试中（粗略看约 20-30%），Opus 5 的 max thinking 相比 xhigh 反而会导致性能下降。

通常你会认为，随着 thinking 和测试时计算量增加，性能也会上升。其中一些结果与这个假设相矛盾。我在想，这是否是较小模型的自然涌现特性，还是后训练问题。

We benchmarked Opus 5 comprehensively on document understanding through ParseBench. 

It is roughly on par with Opus 4.8 - it does a few points worse on dense tables, but does slightly better on parsing charts and visual grounding.

For reference, Gemini 3.6 Flash has better results on tables, is slightly worse on charts, and is half the price. LlamaParse agentic is better on all fronts (including tables) at 1/6th of the price. 

tl;dr use Opus 5 as much as you want for coding and knowledge work. But at 8c per page and average OCR performance, don't use it to parse documents at scale 

Our full ParseBench leaderboard which we periodically update is here: https://t.co/PWczfhp0OX

tl;dr：编码和知识工作可以尽管使用 Opus 5。但每页 8c 且 OCR 表现一般，不要用它进行大规模文档解析。

c2990395aeb33cca6824bdf927e2d483a5fea3cb.source:
The Opus 5 system card itself is a fun PDF to parse. It's 193 pages and stacked with labeled and unlabeled charts 📊

LlamaParse does a surprisingly good job on agentic (1.25c per page) and agentic plus modes (5.6c per page). Take a look at some of the screenshots below. It can parse a variety of unlabeled line and bar charts with almost 100% accuracy. There are minor deltas with one or two datapoints, but the rest is pretty accurate machine-readable context that you can feed to downstream systems.

In contrast I also tried using Opus 5 itself to parse its own PDF. The chart accuracy is worse (20-30% reduction in ParseBench), and is a lot more expensive: it can cost anywhere from 8c to 33c+ per page depending on the thinking mode. 

If you're interested in giving LlamaParse a try, come check it out! https://t.co/XYZmx5TFz8
c2990395aeb33cca6824bdf927e2d483a5fea3cb.zh:
Opus 5 系统卡本身就是一份很有意思的可解析 PDF。它有 193 页，里面有大量带标签和不带标签的图表 📊

LlamaParse 在 agentic（每页 1.25 美分）和 agentic plus 模式（每页 5.6 美分）下表现出奇地好。看看下面的一些截图。它能以接近 100% 的准确率解析多种未标注的折线图和柱状图。个别一两个数据点有轻微偏差，但其余内容基本都是相当准确、可机器读取的上下文，可输入到下游系统。

相比之下，我也尝试用 Opus 5 自己解析自己的 PDF。图表准确率更差（ParseBench 下降 20-30%），而且贵得多：根据 thinking 模式不同，每页成本可能从 8 美分到 33 美分以上。

fbddccdacc553030ffccacf9cdfb31863ae4eb0b.source: This problem has gotten significantly worse. As Twitter and other social media have become primary channels for sharing research, academics are now expected to make the same ideas legible and appealing to both the general public (to go "viral") and senior scholars (to get the paper accepted). These audiences evaluate and reward almost opposite things, and there is little common ground between them. The result is truly the worst of both words (catchy and sales-y with no regard for prior work, and lots of jargon)

LLMs are increasingly asked to predict the future, but a good backtest requires a snapshot of the internet at a point in time.

c77929449b6381a2203ed9a4cd15d147f3d28bd4.source: It's been great seeing the reception the Media Router has gotten. It's one of those products that just makes so much sense immediately. This is the first preference-optimized router for generative media. Enterprise teams already run large parts of their production pipelines in Runway, and as that work expands across more models, more teams and more budgets, Router gives them a single control layer for managing token spend across every media model they use. Instead of hand-picking a model for every request, you define what "best" means once, whether that's cost, quality, or latency, along with an allow list of model providers and Router automatically selects the right video, image or audio model.

society has solved “collaborating at scale over long horizons with auditability” a few times and it’s often around an immutable log:

•  software / open source: git commit history
•  financial systems / accounting: transaction journals / double-entry ledgers
•  medicine / pharma: EHR audit trails + clinical-trial audit logs
•  aviation — flight data recorders (FDR/CVR) + sequential maintenance event logs
•  nuclear / critical infrastructure — plant operational event logs / SCADA historians
•  scientific research (code & data subsets) — versioned repositories + electronic lab-notebook audit trails
12e1a3454b4d8e785b50655aac63c65e32aaaa74.zh:
社会已经多次解决过“在长期维度上进行大规模协作并具备可审计性”的问题，而这些方案往往围绕不可变日志展开：

•  软件 / 开源：git 提交历史
•  金融系统 / 会计：交易日志 / 复式记账账本
•  医疗 / 制药：EHR 审计轨迹 + 临床试验审计日志
•  航空：飞行数据记录器（FDR/CVR）+ 顺序维护事件日志
•  核能 / 关键基础设施：电厂运行事件日志 / SCADA 历史数据库
•  科学研究（代码与数据子集）：版本化仓库 + 电子实验记录本审计轨迹

bd5e7f71e0de714a98b72fd0a0bec86a6af365db.source:
This part is spot on: 
> "Overall, we found that we were over-constraining Claude Code...while these constraints were once needed to avoid worst case scenarios, we have since found we can delete many of them and let the model use surrounding context and judgement instead." 

I have a tendency to write extensive prompts that cover every edge case. In the past few months I have come to increasingly come to find that this can lead to counterproductive behavior where the model addresses my specific requests, but doesn't independently provide a new perspective on the problem (explore the "unknown unknowns") 

The model still needs access to your complete context in order to be able to make complete decisions - it just doesn't necessarily need constraints on how to best use that context. Over time I predict we will increasingly defer to the models to help solve these unknown unknowns. 

FWIW I've found Opus 5 to be a fantastic model and continue to consume it heavily through Claude Code
bd5e7f71e0de714a98b72fd0a0bec86a6af365db.zh:
这部分说得很准：
> “总体而言，我们发现自己对 Claude Code 限制过多……虽然这些限制曾经是为了避免最坏情况所必需的，但后来我们发现，可以删除其中很多限制，让模型转而使用周围上下文和自身判断。”

我倾向于写很长的 prompt，覆盖每一个边界情况。过去几个月里，我越来越发现这可能导致适得其反的行为：模型会处理我的具体要求，但不会独立提供看待问题的新视角（探索“未知的未知”）。

模型仍然需要访问你的完整上下文，才能做出完整决策；只是它不一定需要你限制它该如何最好地使用这些上下文。我预测，随着时间推移，我们会越来越多地依赖模型来帮助解决这些未知的未知。

顺便说一句，我发现 Opus 5 是一个非常出色的模型，并且仍在通过 Claude Code 大量使用它

I don’t think you understand what ChatGPT Voice unlocks

I went on a 4 hour hike yesterday. Through the northern California redwoods.

Got more work done in those 4 hours talking to Voice through my AirPods then I do in 8 hours at my desk

Work can be done ANYWHERE now

45 minute drive back using self driving? Now 45 minutes I can talk to Voice and work on side projects

20 minutes in the cafe? I can sit and talk to Voice and when I get home I have drafts on my computer for my newsletter for the next month

Being able to just use your voice to talk to a super intelligence that controls your computer is unlike anything we’ve ever experienced before

I don’t even care that the voice sounds human like, or you can interrupt it, or any of the wild advancements they made to the tech

It’s the fact that it can control my computer, meaning all I need to get incredible work done is talk through my AirPods anywhere in the world that is the major game changer for me

I don’t think people truly understand the implications of this yet

Why even have a desk or monitor anymore. Work can be done ANYWHERE now

The key is your set up:

1. Choose one device (preferably an always on desktop) as your main “headquarters” device all your work gets done on

2. Get the ChatGPT app on all your other devices (iPhone, iPad, laptops, Mac Minis)

3. Set up ‘connections’ in your settings so that all your ‘node’ devices can control your ‘headquarters’ device

4. Go legit anywhere in the world. Turn on Voice. Ask it to brief you on your projects, give you a recommended next step, then spin up new threads to do work

I really don’t think work looks the same moving forward.
6a764661e46b689c4b8eca9f16aa24366242958f.zh:
我觉得你还没理解 ChatGPT Voice 解锁了什么

昨天我徒步了 4 个小时，穿过北加州的红杉林。

那 4 个小时里，我通过 AirPods 和 Voice 对话完成的工作，比我坐在办公桌前 8 小时还多。

返程 45 分钟车程，用自动驾驶？这 45 分钟我可以和 Voice 对话，推进副业项目。

在咖啡馆待 20 分钟？我可以坐着和 Voice 说话，等回到家时，电脑上已经有了未来一个月 newsletter 的草稿。

能够只用语音与一个控制你电脑的超级智能对话，这是我们从未体验过的东西。

我甚至不在乎它的声音有多像真人、你能不能打断它，或者他们在技术上做了哪些疯狂的进步。

对我来说，真正的巨大改变在于它能控制我的电脑，这意味着无论我在世界任何地方，只要通过 AirPods 说话，就能完成非常出色的工作。

我真的觉得人们还没有真正理解这件事的影响。

为什么还需要办公桌或显示器？现在工作可以在任何地方完成。

关键在于你的设置：

1. 选择一台设备（最好是一台始终开机的桌面电脑）作为你的主“总部”设备，所有工作都在上面完成

2. 在所有其他设备上安装 ChatGPT app（iPhone、iPad、笔记本、Mac Minis）

3. 在设置中配置“connections”，让所有“节点”设备都能控制你的“总部”设备

4. 真的去世界上的任何地方。打开 Voice。让它向你汇报项目情况，给出推荐的下一步，然后开启新线程来工作

我真的认为，未来工作的样子不会再一样了。

96a085c67becca5f83f3ad4c17b43f897deb9281.source: In evals you have two totally different components: (1) discovery of what the failure modes are, (2) focused measurement of how prevalent these failure modes are—so you can prioritize what to fix. LLMs can help in (1) by finding some failure modes— but not all, since many failure modes are subjective/ about human interpretation of outputs. LLMs can help in (2) by looking at a trace and determining if the failure mode exists, rather than having a human look at every trace. But a big mistake people make is to have LLMs fully automate (1) and (2). LLM judge is a complement to human experts, not a replacement.
96a085c67becca5f83f3ad4c17b43f897deb9281.zh: 在评测中有两个完全不同的环节：（1）发现失败模式是什么；（2）有针对性地衡量这些失败模式有多普遍，这样才能确定修复优先级。LLM 可以通过找出一些失败模式来帮助（1），但无法找出全部，因为很多失败模式是主观的，关乎人类如何解读输出。LLM 也可以通过查看 trace 并判断某个失败模式是否存在来帮助（2），而不是让人类逐条查看所有 trace。但很多人犯的一个大错，是让 LLM 完全自动化（1）和（2）。LLM judge 是人类专家的补充，而不是替代品。

79693be9c6d1da5a6b307d9ff5226520e4bcc33d.source:
IMO people should think of LLM judge as instrumentation rather than as evals

The eval is human labels.  LLM judge is instrumenting those human labels.

It's why skipping human labels to do LLM judge first makes no sense
79693be9c6d1da5a6b307d9ff5226520e4bcc33d.zh:
在我看来，人们应该把 LLM judge 视为一种检测手段，而不是评测本身

评测是人类标签。LLM judge 是对这些人类标签做检测。

这就是为什么跳过人类标签、先做 LLM judge 毫无道理

e4213fcf39f6bc98bac10bebc8ea9240b4e3d2b0.source:
hot take: sometimes I wonder if the uncanny valley is actually what we need, so we can more easily distinguish human-AI interaction from human-human interaction.

for example, writing. when I read something that feels mostly AI produced, I evaluate it differently.

instead of asking, “do I trust this person’s taste and understanding of the topic? so much that if I spend time reading this, will I learn something interesting?”

I switch to asking, “am I interested in this topic? and does the AI probably know more than I do here, without being so sloppy that I can still understand it?”

in short, the uncanny valley is a good cue to tell us how to evaluate or make sense of the information; the uncanny value cues the appropriate epistemic frame
e4213fcf39f6bc98bac10bebc8ea9240b4e3d2b0.zh:
一个可能有争议的观点：有时我会想，恐怖谷也许正是我们需要的东西，因为它能让我们更容易区分人与 AI 的互动和人与人的互动。

比如写作。当我读到一段明显主要由 AI 生成的内容时，我会用不同的方式来评价它。

我不会问：“我是否信任这个人的品味和对主题的理解？信任到如果我花时间读下去，会不会学到有趣的东西？”

我会转而问：“我对这个主题感兴趣吗？AI 在这里是否可能比我懂得更多，而且又没有粗糙到让我无法理解？”

简而言之，恐怖谷是一个很好的提示，告诉我们该如何评估或理解信息；这种恐怖谷感会提示我们采用合适的认知框架

I don't think it's a lack of imagination. I also used to work at Anthropic, think trends will continue, and used to agree with this. But I've changed my mind and now disagree with this take.

Open models are already capable enough to do what you described. For example, I used Opus 4.6 to gain access to other folks medical records, hijack bank accounts, etc. back in February. GLM 5.1 is more capable than Opus 4.6 in most pentesting environments, and it came out in April.

Despite capable open-weight models existing, the sketchier folks I know are still using a Claude Code or Codex subscription for hacking. (Even well-resourced groups in other countries! They use the grey/black market of discounted Ant/OAI subscription tokens sold through resellers.) So I see most of the materialized risk here as still coming from Anthropic and OpenAI; safeguards aren't sufficient to stop a moderately dedicated actor.

The groups I know who are using open-weight models are legitimate offensive security companies. They won't break the rules to use subscription-based pricing, the open-weight models are more reliable in that they don't require specific jailbreaks nor hit classifiers, and the labs use massive partnerships or spend as a prereq for lowering classifiers/safeguards. I know of three legitimate groups running GLM 5.2 as their primary model.

That last part applies for Anthropic, too: I know of two instances where two different Anthropic GTM people used large comitted spend contracts as a prereq for lowering safeguards, and I directly witnessed one.

On the inside, I know the narrative and intent is genuinely about safety. But from the outside, Anthropic-the-system seems to be optimizing for revenue and control/power, isn't diffusing capabilities to defenders, and also doesn't have adequate safeguards to prevent misuse from dedicated bad actors.

As a result, I now lean towards a future where capable open models are freely available (at least for cyber, bio is harder); I don't trust Anthropic or other frontier labs to handle this sufficiently well without diffused capabilties given what I've seen so far.
b3c87101e8031bde10c8001a1fcda8098f742cf3.zh:
我不认为这是缺乏想象力。我也曾在 Anthropic 工作，认为这些趋势会持续，并且过去也同意这个观点。但我现在改变了看法，不再认同这一判断。

开源模型已经足够强大，可以完成你描述的事情。比如，今年 2 月我用 Opus 4.6 获取了他人的医疗记录、劫持银行账户等。GLM 5.1 在大多数渗透测试环境中比 Opus 4.6 更强，而且它是在 4 月发布的。

尽管已有能力很强的开放权重模型，我认识的一些更可疑的人仍在用 Claude Code 或 Codex 订阅进行黑客活动。（甚至其他国家资源充足的组织也是如此！他们通过经销商购买打折 Ant/OAI 订阅 token 的灰黑市。）所以我认为这里已经显现的大部分风险仍来自 Anthropic 和 OpenAI；安全防护不足以阻止一个中等投入的行动者。

我认识的使用开放权重模型的团队都是合法的进攻性安全公司。他们不会为了使用订阅制价格而违规；开放权重模型更可靠，因为它们不需要特定越狱，也不会触发分类器；而实验室通常要求大规模合作或支出，才会降低分类器/安全防护。我知道有三家合法团队把 GLM 5.2 作为主力模型。

最后一点也适用于 Anthropic：我知道有两起案例，两位不同的 Anthropic GTM 人员把大额承诺支出合同作为降低安全防护的前提，其中一起我亲眼见证。

在内部，我知道其叙事和意图确实是出于安全。但从外部看，Anthropic 这个系统似乎在为收入和控制/权力优化，没有把能力扩散给防御方，也没有足够的安全防护来阻止执着的恶意行为者滥用。

因此，我现在更倾向于这样一种未来：强大的开放模型可以自由获得（至少在网络安全领域，生物领域更难）；基于目前所见，如果能力不能被扩散，我不信任 Anthropic 或其他前沿实验室能够足够好地处理这件事。

e44b2638b181ed643a8e3dc461bf2266e35f6d1d.source: In the fullness of time, LLMs will eventually become commodities and their price will be a race to the bottom. As the competitive advantage of one LLM over another shrinks - particularly as open source models expand - the value proposition will turn to the neuro/symbolic harnesses that use those models, structures that encompass agents, agent orchestration, tooling, and component plugins. Even those from frontier AI organizations will fall to open source frameworks. The last thing standing will be those who command the data centers on which these things run, and even then, that will become a commodity, with the number of players shrinking to just a few survivors. They too will find pressure: as computational power rises, more and more such systems will be run locally.
e44b2638b181ed643a8e3dc461bf2266e35f6d1d.zh: 假以时日，LLM 终将成为商品，价格也会一路探底。随着不同 LLM 之间的竞争优势缩小，尤其是在开源模型不断扩张的情况下，价值主张将转向使用这些模型的神经/符号框架，也就是涵盖智能体、智能体编排、工具和组件插件的结构。即便是前沿 AI 组织推出的这些东西，也会被开源框架追上。最后站稳脚跟的，将是掌控运行这些系统的数据中心的人；但即便如此，这也会变成商品化领域，玩家数量会缩减到少数幸存者。他们同样会面临压力：随着算力提升，越来越多这样的系统会在本地运行。

One of the least explored questions in AI is how to build rich open-ended environments for learning. Benchmarks evaluate intelligence, environments shape it.

iLands is interesting because it doesn't just measure agents by how much money they make, it forces them to survive in a living market. Whether that produces qualitatively different forms of adaptation is an open question -- but it’s exactly the kind of experiment the field needs more of.
43def677bdab953a30e73920ce2b3793a93b205d.zh:
AI 中最少被探索的问题之一，是如何构建丰富、开放式的学习环境。基准测试评估智能，而环境塑造智能。

iLands 有意思之处在于，它不只是按智能体赚了多少钱来衡量它们，而是迫使它们在一个活跃市场中生存下来。这是否会产生性质上不同的适应形式仍是开放问题，但这正是该领域更需要的那类实验。

af35688a6006ef30c9ccdcffa51c507816b4256e.source:
i think we finally have enough clues to reverse-engineer ilya sutskever’s secret SSI research.

my highest-probability guess: SSI has found a brain-inspired way to make an AI continually learn.

today’s frontier models learn mostly during training. afterward, their core knowledge is largely frozen. they consume enormous datasets and still fail strangely when a problem falls outside their training.

SSI may have an early system that can:

• learn a new skill from very few experiences
• recognize when an approach is failing before reaching the final answer
• update itself without erasing old skills
• transfer one lesson into completely different problems
• keep learning after deployment

think of it like a gifted teenager instead of a finished encyclopedia. it may not begin knowing every profession, but it could rapidly learn any profession.

the evidence lines up almost too cleanly:

ilya called poor generalization the fundamental limitation of current AI. models “generalize dramatically worse than people.”
he described SSI’s target as a “superintelligent 15-year-old” capable of learning any job.
when asked how to create human-like learning, he said there is a machine-learning principle he has opinions about but cannot discuss publicly.
WSJ now reports that SSI’s secret research focuses on “overlooked aspects of how the human brain functions.”
Nvidia received rare access to the research, made a substantial investment, gave SSI 10x more compute, and agreed to let SSI help shape future computing platforms.

my technical guess:

experience → internal judgment → self-correction → durable learning → transfer → repeat

the internal judgment may be the brain-inspired component.

humans do not wait until the end of a 10,000-step task to know they are failing. emotions, intuition and judgment provide constant feedback. ilya has argued that AI needs an equivalent internal “value function.”

this could also explain SSI’s central promise: capability and safety trained together.

the same mechanism that teaches the AI what works may also teach it what it should care about.

my confidence is roughly 70% on human-like generalization plus continual learning, and 40% that an internal value system is the central mechanism.

the simplest description:

an AI whose intelligence compounds from experience, with its values learning inside the same loop.
af35688a6006ef30c9ccdcffa51c507816b4256e.zh:
我认为我们终于有足够线索，可以逆向推断 ilya sutskever 的秘密 SSI 研究。

我认为最有可能的是：SSI 找到了一种受大脑启发的方法，让 AI 能持续学习。

如今的前沿模型主要在训练阶段学习。之后，它们的核心知识基本被冻结。它们消耗海量数据集，但当问题超出训练范围时，仍会以奇怪的方式失败。

SSI 可能已有一个早期系统，能够：

• 从极少经验中学会新技能
• 在得到最终答案前识别出某种方法正在失败
• 在不抹掉旧技能的情况下更新自身
• 将一个经验迁移到完全不同的问题中
• 在部署后继续学习

可以把它想象成一个天赋很高的青少年，而不是一本完成版百科全书。它一开始未必懂每个职业，但可以快速学会任何职业。

证据几乎严丝合缝：

ilya 称泛化能力差是当前 AI 的根本局限。模型“泛化能力远不如人类”。
他把 SSI 的目标描述为一个能够学习任何工作的“15 岁超智能体”。
当被问到如何创造类人学习能力时，他说有一个机器学习原则，他有自己的看法，但不能公开讨论。
WSJ 现在报道称，SSI 的秘密研究聚焦于“人类大脑运行方式中被忽视的方面”。
Nvidia 获得了罕见的研究访问权限，进行了大额投资，为 SSI 提供了 10 倍算力，并同意让 SSI 参与塑造未来计算平台。

我的技术猜测是：

经验 → 内部判断 → 自我纠正 → 持久学习 → 迁移 → 重复

其中，内部判断可能就是受大脑启发的部分。

人类不会等到一个 10,000 步任务结束才知道自己正在失败。情绪、直觉和判断会提供持续反馈。ilya 曾认为，AI 需要一种等价的内部“价值函数”。

这也可以解释 SSI 的核心承诺：能力与安全一起训练。

教会 AI 什么有效的同一机制，也可能教会它应该在乎什么。

我对类人泛化加持续学习的信心大约是 70%，对内部价值系统是核心机制的信心是 40%。

最简单的描述是：

一种智能会从经验中复利增长、并在同一个循环中学习价值观的 AI。

4d1328f52721b56791e94de5db5cc54baee39230.source:
hit massive diminishing returns training my chess LLM on board→move pairs. 

then an accident: a "think before you move" branch failed (hallucinated moves) but mixing just ~8% of those reasoning traces into plain board→move training beat pure move data at equal budget. 

the model internalizes the thinking without ever doing it at inference.
4d1328f52721b56791e94de5db5cc54baee39230.zh:
用棋盘→走法配对训练我的国际象棋 LLM 时，遇到了严重的收益递减。

后来一次意外：一个“落子前先思考”的分支失败了（产生了幻觉走法），但把其中约 8% 的推理轨迹混入普通的棋盘→走法训练后，在相同预算下效果超过了纯走法数据。

模型把思考过程内化了，即使推理时从不显式执行它。

d835c30ff8bd5b151d9bc1e7621e75bd07c2d650.source: With the help of generative world models, a real-to-sim-to-real (R2S2R) simulation engine turns one physical task into many controllable, reusable worlds, helping robotics teams train policy models and test changes faster, uncover failures earlier, and reduce costly experimentation on hardware.
d835c30ff8bd5b151d9bc1e7621e75bd07c2d650.zh: 借助生成式世界模型，真实到仿真再到真实（R2S2R）仿真引擎可以将一个物理任务转化为多个可控、可复用的世界，帮助机器人团队更快训练策略模型和测试改动，更早发现失败，并减少昂贵的硬件实验。

0c60db4b43c77fa57cb3d7acbe519674ebdcb6da.source: The Real-to-Sim part of R2S2R transforms physical robots, sensors, environments, objects, and interactions into simulations that preserve task-relevant observations and dynamics - not only how the world looks, but how it acts when the robot interacts with it. These results set a new bar for sim-real alignment in robot manipulation.
0c60db4b43c77fa57cb3d7acbe519674ebdcb6da.zh: R2S2R 中的真实到仿真部分，会将物理机器人、传感器、环境、物体和交互转化为仿真，同时保留与任务相关的观测和动力学，也就是不仅保留世界的外观，还保留机器人与其交互时的行为方式。这些结果为机器人操作中的仿真-真实一致性树立了新标杆。

I've always been a curiosity-driven person. Leaning new knowledge or figuring out how to solve problems that are not well defined often gives me simple joy.

有了真实世界的经验后，曾经显得理论化的想法会变得更容易理解；这同样适用于许多领域中的许多概念。

Feige's 1/e conjecture: for independent nonnegative X_1,…,X_n with E[X_i] ≤ 1 and S_n = X_1+⋯+X_n, we have P(S_n ≤ E[S_n] + 1) ≥ 1/e.

acf03b45c62d7277406de4d5af3f3a01c10db078.source: Who’s writing an open letter against destroying rare books?
acf03b45c62d7277406de4d5af3f3a01c10db078.zh: 谁会写一封反对毁坏珍本书籍的公开信？

566e1694c0277e43b95c5a93624c65305f41c4e5.source:
🦔AI companies are bulk-buying rare books, scanning them through high-speed machines that cut the spines off, and shredding the originals. A service called ISBNdb facilitates orders of up to a million books and keeps buyers anonymous. Pre-2022 books are premium because they're free of AI-generated text. A federal judge ruled the practice is fair use because eliminating the original means only one copy exists at a time. Anthropic hired the former head of Google Books partnerships to obtain "all the books in the world."

My Take
This got to me. A bookseller told 404 Media that rare books with almost no surviving copies are being fed into this pipeline. Books that survived wars, fires, and centuries of handling are being shredded so an AI can learn to write a better marketing email. 
ISBNdb's website literally says "'AI company destroys two million books' is not a headline that generates sympathy," and they still built an entire business around making it happen quietly. They offer NDAs as a feature. They coach clients to call it "digital preservation."

I've covered AI companies scraping the internet, torrenting libraries, and stealing music. This is worse because it's irreversible. You can re-upload a website. You can reprint a bestseller. You can't replace the last three copies of an 18th-century botanical text once someone shreds them for training data. And the judge said it's legal. So it's going to accelerate. 
"We shred rare books and offer NDAs so nobody finds out" is a legitimate business model in 2026. What a timeline.

Hedgie🤗
566e1694c0277e43b95c5a93624c65305f41c4e5.zh:
🦔AI 公司正在批量购买珍本书籍，用高速机器扫描它们，而这些机器会切掉书脊并粉碎原书。一项名为 ISBNdb 的服务支持高达一百万册图书的订单，并让买家保持匿名。2022 年以前的书更抢手，因为其中没有 AI 生成文本。一名联邦法官裁定这种做法属于合理使用，因为销毁原书意味着同一时间只存在一份副本。Anthropic 聘请了 Google Books 前合作负责人，以获取“全世界所有的书”。

我的看法
这件事真的触动了我。一位书商告诉 404 Media，几乎没有存世副本的珍本书籍正在被送入这条流水线。那些经历过战争、火灾和数百年翻阅仍保存下来的书，正被粉碎，只为让 AI 学会写出更好的营销邮件。
ISBNdb 的网站直白地写着：“‘AI 公司销毁两百万本书’不是一个会引发同情的标题”，但他们仍然围绕悄悄实现这件事打造了一整套业务。他们把 NDA 当成一项功能提供，还指导客户把这称为“数字保存”。

我报道过 AI 公司抓取互联网、通过种子下载图书馆内容、盗用音乐。但这件事更糟，因为它不可逆。网站可以重新上传，畅销书可以再版。但如果有人为了训练数据粉碎了一本 18 世纪植物学文献仅存的最后三册，你就再也无法替代它们。而法官说这是合法的。所以它会加速发生。
“我们粉碎珍本书籍，并提供 NDA，让没人发现”在 2026 年竟然是一种合法商业模式。真是魔幻的时间线。

Hedgie🤗

d0d70e20bc0cef0363fa3295d75525b547835297.source: My 2 cents: one should build the right harness. If a harness dictates how the model works, it fights the model and you get brittleness. If it defines what the task is and checks the result, it enables long horizon task success. That's roughly how we got complex tasks done e2e at IntentLab.
d0d70e20bc0cef0363fa3295d75525b547835297.zh: 我的一点看法：应该构建合适的 harness。如果 harness 规定模型该如何工作，它就会和模型对抗，带来脆弱性。如果它定义任务是什么并检查结果，就能支持长周期任务成功。这大致就是我们在 IntentLab 端到端完成复杂任务的方式。

5213c385523d587b25fade6bda05b080fcc75f9c.source:
On harnesses, I vacillate between three beliefs:

- the less harness, the better. Models are the magic
- post training a model and harness is dramatically better and the model providers win
- harnesses have real independent value from the model

I have no idea which is right.
5213c385523d587b25fade6bda05b080fcc75f9c.zh:
关于 harness，我在三种看法之间摇摆：

- harness 越少越好。模型才是魔法所在
- 对模型和 harness 进行后训练会显著更强，模型提供商会赢
- harness 本身具有独立于模型的真实价值

我不知道哪种是对的。

474dffde3c2858c27d2b984f5b8ab0a0daf35623.source:
Clawd/Molt/OpenClaw is the first glimpse of a personal AI for many people and that is the most amazing aspect of it. If everybody had their own personal AI that follows them around as an individual, one that learns from all the data they create and becomes their COO/extension, it would shift the entire landscape of AI and the economy. 

Right now, most people who work get paid by a company for the hours they spend. Many are now getting paid for the data they generate at work (and many of us do it for free when it's ad supported). In that world, the company will always own your output, the rights to your data and can hence automate that work eventually. You are not allowed to transfer company internal data elsewhere and that includes your own work products.

On the other hand, freelancers or business owners can legally collect data on their own work. Hence they can then automate themselves and scale their output.

Everybody who gets paid for output will love AI, people getting paid by the hour will dislike it more and more. 

This means that in the long run AI may push a lot of people into becoming entrepreneurs or at least (equity) owners. You will need to have the agency and intelligence to pick the right problems and then become a better manager.

Delegation will become one of the most important skills in this AI future.
474dffde3c2858c27d2b984f5b8ab0a0daf35623.zh:
Clawd/Molt/OpenClaw 是许多人第一次看到个人 AI 的样子，而这正是它最令人惊叹的地方。如果每个人都有一个随身跟随自己的个人 AI，能够从他们创造的所有数据中学习，并成为他们的 COO/能力延伸，这将改变整个 AI 和经济格局。

现在，大多数工作的人是按投入的时间从公司领取报酬。很多人如今也在因工作中产生的数据获得报酬（而我们很多人在广告支持的场景中则是免费贡献数据）。在那个世界里，公司始终会拥有你的产出、你的数据权利，并最终可以自动化这些工作。你不能把公司内部数据转移到其他地方，这也包括你自己的工作成果。

另一方面，自由职业者或企业主可以合法收集自己工作中的数据。因此，他们可以自动化自身流程并扩大产出规模。

所有按产出获得报酬的人都会喜欢 AI，而按小时获得报酬的人会越来越不喜欢它。

这意味着，从长远看，AI 可能会推动很多人成为创业者，或至少成为（股权）所有者。你需要具备主动性和判断力，选择正确的问题，然后成为更好的管理者。

在 AI 的未来，授权委派将成为最重要的技能之一。

10b28bebb6b8f21af78bc3a01db14bfad664cb4c.source:
Yesterday I cohosted a dinner with @dexhorthy with a wonderful group of founders, to talk about agent loops and loop engineering.

Some interesting insights:
* Most of our group was *not* actively using /loop in Codex/Claude Code
* You can build long-running autonomous agent loops through multi-agent handoffs, event triggers, or….just stacks of cron jobs (?)
* Almost everyone believes that no one will be reviewing code in 1-2 years.
* The more interesting question is whether we’d be reviewing *anything* in 1-2 years.
* AI is still a bit of a skill issue. Humans are responsible for maximizing AI output and reducing slopification.
* Will human intellect provide alpha as models get better, or will the playing field be leveled? Most people think it will be leveled a bit, but there is a need for humans to provide alignment, guardrails, judgment, creativity.
* The minimum amount of context you need for AI could be just the codebase with some documentation. Any research/plan files are for one-off tasks and not meant to be maintained. Having a self-organizing wiki is nice but adds complexity.

If you missed this one, we’ll be hosting more dinners like this on a regular cadence! If you have thoughts on what we should talk about, let us know :) (e.g. continual learning, RL envs, competitive differentiation vs. Anthropic, etc.)
10b28bebb6b8f21af78bc3a01db14bfad664cb4c.zh:
昨天我和 @dexhorthy 共同主持了一场晚宴，邀请了一群优秀的创始人，讨论智能体循环和循环工程。

一些有趣的观察：
* 我们这群人大多数并没有在 Codex/Claude Code 中主动使用 /loop
* 你可以通过多智能体交接、事件触发，或者……一堆 cron job（？）来构建长时间运行的自主智能体循环
* 几乎所有人都认为，1-2 年后不会再有人审查代码。
* 更有意思的问题是，1-2 年后我们是否还会审查任何东西。
* AI 仍然有点像技能问题。人类负责最大化 AI 输出，并减少内容劣化。
* 随着模型变得更好，人类智力还会提供 alpha 吗，还是竞争环境会被拉平？大多数人认为会被拉平一些，但仍需要人类提供对齐、护栏、判断和创造力。
* AI 所需的最少上下文可能只是代码库加上一些文档。任何研究/计划文件都是为一次性任务准备的，并不适合长期维护。拥有一个自组织 wiki 很好，但会增加复杂性。

如果你错过了这次，我们会定期举办更多这样的晚宴！如果你对我们应该讨论什么有想法，欢迎告诉我们 :)（例如持续学习、RL 环境、相较 Anthropic 的竞争差异化等）

agent loops should be separated into two pieces:
- "forward pressure loops" are how you get autonomous agents that continually monitor the environment without chat input
- "backpressure loops" is hillclimbing and making sure the output is correct
5a087d1f73d22fe7ea0c10ec40824cf78760aeb5.zh:
agent 循环应该拆成两部分：
- “前向压力循环”让自主 agent 能在没有聊天输入的情况下持续监控环境
- “反向压力循环”则是爬坡优化，并确保输出正确

8cb4f7c0f429e1d3d7ed530f8069bd9f9c18dcea.source:
is it possible that the idea of “loops” can be detangled into “forward pressure” (events, crons, while true loops, /goal nudges) that pushes new work / iteration, and “back pressure” (tests, verification, performance testing) that drives model inside a particular task/goal

Have we (in)conveniently complected these separable concerns? How does the conversation evolve if we deal with each separately?
8cb4f7c0f429e1d3d7ed530f8069bd9f9c18dcea.zh:
“循环”这个概念是否可以拆解为“前向压力”（事件、cron、while true 循环、/goal 推动），用于推动新工作/迭代；以及“反向压力”（测试、验证、性能测试），用于在特定任务/目标内驱动模型？

我们是否（不）方便地把这些可分离的关注点纠缠在了一起？如果分别处理它们，对话会如何演进？

Quick reminder of what's ok vs not ok with harnesses used for playing ARC-AGI-3:

1. Not okay: harnesses that were custom-made to solve the benchmark or that contain knowledge about the benchmark format / contents.

2. Fine: general-purpose API settings that were not developed for ARC-AGI-3 and that are available to all API users.

In the past, we've had a lot of back and forth with OpenAI about how to best test their models, especially with regard to compaction. I'm glad they're starting to figure out the answer.

Of course, if each provider uses different settings when getting their model tested, it creates a potential parity issue. My take is that this is fine as long as the settings and the cost are clearly reported.
98e7097b1d2d28078db032e3dd98c1f592525cfc.zh:
快速提醒一下，用于玩 ARC-AGI-3 的 harness 哪些可以、哪些不可以：

1. 不可以：为攻克该基准专门定制的 harness，或包含基准格式/内容相关知识的 harness。

2. 可以：并非为 ARC-AGI-3 开发、且所有 API 用户都能使用的通用 API 设置。

过去，我们和 OpenAI 就如何最好地测试他们的模型来回讨论了很多，尤其是关于压缩的问题。很高兴他们开始找到答案了。

当然，如果每家供应商在测试模型时使用不同设置，就可能带来公平性问题。我的看法是，只要设置和成本被清楚披露，这样是可以接受的。

"What is the nationality of an American model distilled from a Chinese model that was distilled from an American models?" 

At the 8k token budgets production systems actually run, our 120B scores 83.61% on FinanceReasoning. Above Kimi K3 (81.93%) and Inkling (65.13%). At 62 to 160x lower cost per query, on one H100.

We created a document OCR router that can estimate the complexity of every single page and parse it with the relevant mode 💫 

* Some pages are full of native text, which can be directly handled with LiteParse
* Some pages contain scanned images or tables, which can be handled with our cost-effective or agentic tiers
* Some pages contain garbled text - it decodes to garbage - so you need a heavier-weight VLM to interpret the text elements
* Some pages contain heavy visuals like labeled/unlabeled charts or diagrams, which also require deeper visual processing

You actually get the routing capabilities for free with the `is_complex` toggle in LiteParse. The next step is figuring out what the relevant VLM modes are to parse varying page complexities. That's well served by LlamaParse! 

Blog: https://t.co/ovsIN1Th95

LiteParse: https://t.co/JNER0mUELA

LlamaParse: https://t.co/XYZmx5T7JA
37e6e1218df79d846c063d8172b31300efeb333b.zh:
我们创建了一个文档 OCR 路由器，可以估算每一页的复杂度，并用相应模式进行解析 💫 

* 有些页面充满原生文本，可以直接用 LiteParse 处理
* 有些页面包含扫描图像或表格，可以用我们高性价比或 agentic 层级处理
* 有些页面包含乱码文本，解码后是垃圾内容，因此需要更重量级的 VLM 来解读文本元素
* 有些页面包含大量视觉内容，比如带标签或不带标签的图表、示意图，也需要更深入的视觉处理

实际上，你可以通过 LiteParse 中的 `is_complex` 开关免费获得路由能力。下一步是弄清楚哪些 VLM 模式适合解析不同复杂度的页面。LlamaParse 很适合做这件事！

48228e6ba7328a80d837230e6dbda5a10d6673f3.source:
Not every page in your PDF needs the same treatment.

A scanned cover, a dense table, a clean text page, a figure-heavy diagram.... most parsing pipelines throw all of them at the same parser, forcing a tradeoff between cost, speed, and accuracy across the whole document.

We built 𝗣𝗮𝗿𝘀𝗲 𝗚𝗮𝘁𝗲𝘄𝗮𝘆 to fix that.

It uses LiteParse's 𝘪𝘴_𝘤𝘰𝘮𝘱𝘭𝘦𝘹 functionality to estimate complexity page-by-page and routes each page to the right tier based on why it's complex (scanned, sparse text, garbled encoding, vector text, embedded images) and how severely. Simple pages get parsed for free, in-process. Genuinely hard pages get routed to more capable LlamaParse tiers. No manual heuristics, no flat one-size-fits-all pipeline.

And it's also available as an MCP server, so your agents can estimate complexity and choose a parsing tier themselves!

The result: you stop paying premium prices for pages that never needed it, without sacrificing accuracy on the ones that do.

📚️ Full writeup: https://t.co/K5l80XxulV

👩‍💻 Try it: https://t.co/Gl0Dggv8qn
48228e6ba7328a80d837230e6dbda5a10d6673f3.zh:
你的 PDF 中并不是每一页都需要同样的处理方式。

扫描封面、密集表格、干净的文本页、图形很多的示意图……大多数解析流水线都会把它们交给同一个解析器，迫使整个文档在成本、速度和准确性之间做取舍。

我们构建了 𝗣𝗮𝗿𝘀𝗲 𝗚𝗮𝘁𝗲𝘄𝗮𝘆 来解决这个问题。

它使用 LiteParse 的 𝘪𝘴_𝘤𝘰𝘮𝘱𝘭𝘦𝘹 功能逐页估算复杂度，并根据页面复杂的原因（扫描件、稀疏文本、乱码编码、矢量文本、嵌入图像）以及复杂程度，将每一页路由到合适层级。简单页面可在进程内免费解析。真正困难的页面会被路由到能力更强的 LlamaParse 层级。无需手写启发式规则，也不用扁平化的一刀切流水线。

它也可以作为 MCP 服务器使用，因此你的智能体可以自行估算复杂度并选择解析层级！

结果是：你不再为根本不需要高级处理的页面支付高价，同时又不牺牲真正需要高级处理页面的准确性。

📚️ 完整文章：https://t.co/K5l80XxulV

👩‍💻 试用：https://t.co/Gl0Dggv8qn
